Hyperparameter Exploration: Learning Rate, Optimiser, and Batch Size¶

DATA425 / STATS448 | Assignment 3 Q3

This notebook trains fully connected networks on a challenging image classification dataset and systematically varies three hyperparameters to observe their effect on training dynamics:

  1. Learning rate — too high, too small, and sensible
  2. Optimiser — SGD, RMSProp, Adam
  3. Batch size — mini-batch vs full-batch gradient descent

Each experiment keeps all other settings fixed and changes only the hyperparameter under study.

# ── Dataset selection ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATASET = "cifar10"       # "cifar10" | "fashion_mnist"
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def load_dataset(name, val_fraction=0.15, random_state=SEED):
    """
    Load and normalise one of two challenging datasets.

    cifar10       : 60,000 images, 32×32 RGB,       10 classes
    fashion_mnist : 70,000 images, 28×28 greyscale, 10 classes

    Returns
    -------
    dict with keys: X_train, y_train, X_val, y_val, X_test, y_test,
                    input_shape, num_classes
    """
    name = name.lower()
    if name == "cifar10":
        (X_tr, y_tr), (X_test, y_test) = keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
        class_names = ["airplane","automobile","bird","cat","deer",
                       "dog","frog","horse","ship","truck"]
    elif name == "fashion_mnist":
        (X_tr, y_tr), (X_test, y_test) = keras.datasets.fashion_mnist.load_data()
        class_names = ["T-shirt","Trouser","Pullover","Dress","Coat",
                       "Sandal","Shirt","Sneaker","Bag","Ankle boot"]
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown dataset '{name}'. Choose: cifar10 | fashion_mnist")

    X_tr   = X_tr.astype("float32")   / 255.0
    X_test = X_test.astype("float32") / 255.0
    y_tr   = y_tr.astype("int64").ravel()
    y_test = y_test.astype("int64").ravel()

    X_train, X_val, y_train, y_val = train_test_split(
        X_tr, y_tr, test_size=val_fraction,
        random_state=random_state, stratify=y_tr
    )

    input_shape = X_train.shape[1:]
    num_classes = int(np.unique(y_tr).size)

    print(f"Dataset      : {name}")
    print(f"Input shape  : {input_shape}")
    print(f"Classes      : {num_classes}  {class_names}")
    print(f"Train        : {X_train.shape[0]:,}")
    print(f"Val          : {X_val.shape[0]:,}")
    print(f"Test         : {X_test.shape[0]:,}")

    return dict(X_train=X_train, y_train=y_train,
                X_val=X_val,     y_val=y_val,
                X_test=X_test,   y_test=y_test,
                input_shape=input_shape, num_classes=num_classes,
                class_names=class_names)


ds = load_dataset(DATASET)

X_train, y_train = ds["X_train"], ds["y_train"]
X_val,   y_val   = ds["X_val"],   ds["y_val"]
X_test,  y_test  = ds["X_test"],  ds["y_test"]
INPUT_SHAPE      = ds["input_shape"]
NUM_CLASSES      = ds["num_classes"]
CLASS_NAMES      = ds["class_names"]

# ── sample grid ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
n_show = 10
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n_show, figsize=(12, 2))
for ax, img, lbl in zip(axes, X_train[:n_show], y_train[:n_show]):
    ax.imshow(img, cmap="gray" if img.ndim == 2 else None)
    ax.set_title(CLASS_NAMES[lbl], fontsize=8)
    ax.axis("off")
plt.suptitle(f"{DATASET}  —  sample images", y=1.05)

1. Learning Rate¶

The learning rate $\eta$ controls how large each gradient descent step is:

$$w \leftarrow w - \eta \cdot \nabla L(w)$$

Three qualitatively different regimes exist regardless of the dataset or network:

Regime What happens
Too small Loss decreases but very slowly — the network is barely learning each epoch
Sensible Loss drops steadily and smoothly — the network converges efficiently
Too large Loss bounces around or diverges — the optimiser overshoots the minimum every step

The experiment below trains the same network architecture three times with plain SGD, changing only the learning rate. Everything else — architecture, epochs, batch size, random seed — is held constant.

In [74]:
import json, pathlib

# ── Learning rate values — edit these to experiment ──────────────────────────
LR_TOO_SMALL = 0.0005   # barely moves        — very slow convergence
LR_SENSIBLE  = 0.01     # steady descent      — efficient learning
LR_TOO_LARGE = 0.15     # overshoots/diverges — bounces or flatlines
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

EPOCHS     = 30
BATCH_SIZE = 128

LR_CONFIGS = {
    f"too small  (lr = {LR_TOO_SMALL})": LR_TOO_SMALL,
    f"sensible   (lr = {LR_SENSIBLE})":  LR_SENSIBLE,
    f"too large  (lr = {LR_TOO_LARGE})": LR_TOO_LARGE,
}

def _lr_str(v): return str(v).replace(".", "p")
def _safe(label):
    return label.replace(" ", "_").replace("=", "").replace(".", "p").replace("(","").replace(")","")

SAVE_DIR = pathlib.Path(
    f"saved/lr_experiment/s{_lr_str(LR_TOO_SMALL)}_m{_lr_str(LR_SENSIBLE)}_l{_lr_str(LR_TOO_LARGE)}"
)

# ── callback: evaluates on test set at the end of every epoch ─────────────────
class TestAccHistory(keras.callbacks.Callback):
    def __init__(self, X_test, y_test):
        super().__init__()
        self.X_test   = X_test
        self.y_test   = y_test
        self.test_accs = []

    def on_epoch_end(self, epoch, logs=None):
        _, acc = self.model.evaluate(self.X_test, self.y_test, verbose=0)
        self.test_accs.append(float(acc))

# ── cache check — also invalidates if per-epoch test data is missing ──────────
_results_file = SAVE_DIR / "lr_results.json"
_model_files  = [SAVE_DIR / f"model_{_safe(l)}.keras" for l in LR_CONFIGS]

def _cache_valid():
    if not (_results_file.exists() and all(p.exists() for p in _model_files)):
        return False
    with open(_results_file) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    # invalidate if any entry is missing per-epoch test accuracy
    return all("test_acc_per_epoch" in v for v in data.values())

if _cache_valid():
    print(f"Saved results found — loading from  {SAVE_DIR}\n")
    with open(_results_file) as f:
        lr_results = json.load(f)
    lr_models = {l: keras.models.load_model(SAVE_DIR / f"model_{_safe(l)}.keras")
                 for l in lr_results}
    EPOCHS = len(lr_results[next(iter(lr_results))]["loss"])
    for label, hist in lr_results.items():
        print(f"  {label:<32}  test_acc = {hist['test_accuracy']:.3f}")

else:
    print("No saved results (or missing per-epoch test data) — training from scratch.\n")

    def build_model(learning_rate):
        tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(SEED)
        model = keras.Sequential([
            keras.Input(shape=INPUT_SHAPE),
            layers.Flatten(),
            layers.Dense(256, activation="relu"),
            layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"),
            layers.Dense(NUM_CLASSES, activation="softmax"),
        ], name=f"lr_{_lr_str(learning_rate)}")
        model.compile(
            optimizer=keras.optimizers.SGD(learning_rate=learning_rate),
            loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
            metrics=["accuracy"],
        )
        return model

    lr_results, lr_models = {}, {}
    for label, lr in LR_CONFIGS.items():
        print(f"Training: {label} ...", end=" ", flush=True)
        cb    = TestAccHistory(X_test, y_test)
        model = build_model(lr)
        hist  = model.fit(X_train, y_train,
                          validation_data=(X_val, y_val),
                          epochs=EPOCHS, batch_size=BATCH_SIZE,
                          callbacks=[cb], verbose=0)
        _, test_acc = model.evaluate(X_test, y_test, verbose=0)
        lr_results[label] = hist.history
        lr_results[label]["test_accuracy"]     = test_acc
        lr_results[label]["test_acc_per_epoch"] = cb.test_accs
        lr_models[label] = model
        print(f"done  (val_acc = {hist.history['val_accuracy'][-1]:.3f}  |  test_acc = {test_acc:.3f})")

    SAVE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(_results_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump(lr_results, f)
    for label, model in lr_models.items():
        model.save(SAVE_DIR / f"model_{_safe(label)}.keras")
    print(f"\nSaved to  {SAVE_DIR.resolve()}")

  sensible   (lr = 0.01)            test_acc = 0.419
  too large  (lr = 0.15)            test_acc = 0.433

# ── Graph 4: Loss surface — gradient descent paths (toy 1-D parabola) ─────────
#
# Purely illustrative — not derived from the dataset.
# A toy parabola L(w) = (w - W_OPT)^2 + L_MIN is used so the loss surface
# can be drawn in 2-D.  The three learning rates below are chosen to clearly
# show the three visual regimes; they are NOT the network training LRs above.

W_OPT = 3.0          # minimum of the parabola
L_MIN = 1.0          # loss at the minimum
W_INIT = -2.0        # shared starting point for all three paths
STEPS = 25           # gradient descent steps to trace

TOY_LR_SMALL    = 0.05    # slow — many tiny steps
TOY_LR_SENSIBLE = 0.30    # steady — converges in ~5 steps
TOY_LR_LARGE    = 0.90    # overshoots — bounces across the minimum

def _toy_loss(w): return (w - W_OPT) ** 2 + L_MIN
def _toy_grad(w): return 2.0 * (w - W_OPT)

toy_configs = {
    f"too small  (lr = {TOY_LR_SMALL})":    (TOY_LR_SMALL,    "#1f77b4"),
    f"sensible   (lr = {TOY_LR_SENSIBLE})": (TOY_LR_SENSIBLE, "#2ca02c"),
    f"too large  (lr = {TOY_LR_LARGE})":    (TOY_LR_LARGE,    "#d62728"),
}

w_range = np.linspace(-2.8, 7.5, 400)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(w_range, _toy_loss(w_range), color="black", linewidth=2.5, label="loss curve")

for label, (lr, col) in toy_configs.items():
    w = W_INIT
    ws = [w]
    for _ in range(STEPS):
        w = w - lr * _toy_grad(w)
        ws.append(w)
    ws = np.array(ws)
    ax.plot(ws, _toy_loss(ws), color=col, linewidth=1.5,
            marker="o", markersize=4, label=label)

ax.set_xlabel("w")
ax.set_ylabel("loss")
ax.set_title("Gradient descent depends on the learning rate\n"
             "Conceptual illustration — toy 1-D parabola, not derived from data")
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
In [79]:
# ── Graph 4b: Same paths via tf.GradientTape (automatic differentiation) ──────
#
# Identical setup to Graph 4 — same toy parabola, same W_INIT, same toy LRs.
# Gradients are now computed by TF autodiff rather than the analytic formula.
# Paths should be numerically identical, confirming autodiff == hand-calc.
# Also purely illustrative — not derived from the dataset.

_W_OPT_tf = tf.constant(W_OPT, dtype=tf.float32)
_L_MIN_tf  = tf.constant(L_MIN, dtype=tf.float32)

def _toy_loss_tf(w_var):
    return (w_var - _W_OPT_tf) ** 2 + _L_MIN_tf

def _run_gd_tf(w_init, lr, steps=STEPS):
    w   = tf.Variable(float(w_init), dtype=tf.float32)
    opt = keras.optimizers.SGD(learning_rate=lr)
    ws  = [float(w.numpy())]
    for _ in range(steps):
        with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
            loss = _toy_loss_tf(w)
        grads = tape.gradient(loss, [w])
        opt.apply_gradients(zip(grads, [w]))
        ws.append(float(w.numpy()))
    return np.array(ws)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(w_range, _toy_loss(w_range), color="black", linewidth=2.5, label="loss curve")

for label, (lr, col) in toy_configs.items():
    ws = _run_gd_tf(W_INIT, lr)
    ax.plot(ws, _toy_loss(ws), color=col, linewidth=1.5,
            marker="o", markersize=4, label=label)

ax.set_xlabel("w")
ax.set_ylabel("loss")
ax.set_title("Gradient descent depends on the learning rate\n"
             "tf.GradientTape (autodiff) — conceptual illustration, not derived from data")
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Observations:

  • Too small (0.0005): Loss decreases very slowly across all 30 epochs. The network is learning but barely — each gradient step is so tiny that it takes many more epochs to approach a useful solution. Validation accuracy remains low.
  • Sensible (0.01): Loss drops steadily from the first epoch and continues to fall smoothly. Validation accuracy climbs consistently — this is the well-behaved regime where gradient descent works as intended.
  • Too large (0.5): Loss is erratic from the start — it may spike, flatline near log(10) ≈ 2.3, or oscillate without improving. The optimiser overshoots the minimum on every step, so the network fails to learn.

This matches exactly the three gradient descent regimes shown in the loss-surface visualisation: too-small steps inch left slowly, the sensible rate descends the parabola cleanly, and the too-large rate bounces across the minimum.

2. Optimiser¶

The optimiser decides how gradient information is used to update weights each step.

Optimiser Key idea
SGD Raw gradient scaled by a single learning rate — simple but can be slow or sensitive to the LR choice
RMSProp Divides each update by a running average of recent squared gradients — adapts the step size per parameter
Adam Combines RMSProp's per-parameter scaling with momentum — usually the most reliable default

Everything below is held fixed: same architecture, same dataset, same batch size, same number of epochs. Only the optimiser changes.

In [80]:
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix

# ── Optimiser hyperparameters — edit these to experiment ─────────────────────
OPT_LR_SGD     = 0.01     # SGD learning rate  (same as LR_SENSIBLE above)
OPT_LR_RMSPROP = 0.001    # RMSProp learning rate  (standard default)
OPT_LR_ADAM    = 0.001    # Adam learning rate     (standard default)
OPT_MOMENTUM   = 0.9      # momentum for SGD only
OPT_EPOCHS     = 30
OPT_BATCH_SIZE = 128
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

_OPT_NAMES   = ["SGD", "RMSProp", "Adam"]
_OPT_COLOURS = {"SGD": "#1f77b4", "RMSProp": "#ff7f0e", "Adam": "#2ca02c"}
_OPT_DISPLAY = {
    "SGD":     f"SGD      (lr={OPT_LR_SGD}, momentum={OPT_MOMENTUM})",
    "RMSProp": f"RMSProp  (lr={OPT_LR_RMSPROP})",
    "Adam":    f"Adam     (lr={OPT_LR_ADAM})",
}

def _make_opt(name):
    if name == "SGD":
        return keras.optimizers.SGD(learning_rate=OPT_LR_SGD, momentum=OPT_MOMENTUM)
    if name == "RMSProp":
        return keras.optimizers.RMSprop(learning_rate=OPT_LR_RMSPROP)
    return keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=OPT_LR_ADAM)

OPT_SAVE_DIR = pathlib.Path(
    f"saved/opt_experiment/"
    f"sgd{_lr_str(OPT_LR_SGD)}_rms{_lr_str(OPT_LR_RMSPROP)}_adam{_lr_str(OPT_LR_ADAM)}"
)

_opt_results_file = OPT_SAVE_DIR / "opt_results.json"
_opt_model_files  = [OPT_SAVE_DIR / f"model_{n}.keras" for n in _OPT_NAMES]

def _opt_cache_valid():
    if not (_opt_results_file.exists() and all(p.exists() for p in _opt_model_files)):
        return False
    with open(_opt_results_file) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return all("test_acc_per_epoch" in v and "test_predictions" in v for v in data.values())

if _opt_cache_valid():
    print(f"Saved results found — loading from  {OPT_SAVE_DIR}\n")
    with open(_opt_results_file) as f:
        opt_results = json.load(f)
    opt_models = {n: keras.models.load_model(OPT_SAVE_DIR / f"model_{n}.keras")
                  for n in _OPT_NAMES}
    OPT_EPOCHS = len(opt_results[next(iter(opt_results))]["val_accuracy"])
    for name, hist in opt_results.items():
        print(f"  {name:<10}  test_acc = {hist['test_accuracy']:.3f}")

else:
    print("No saved results — training from scratch.\n")

    def _build_opt_model():
        tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(SEED)
        m = keras.Sequential([
            keras.Input(shape=INPUT_SHAPE),
            layers.Flatten(),
            layers.Dense(256, activation="relu"),
            layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"),
            layers.Dense(NUM_CLASSES, activation="softmax"),
        ])
        return m

    opt_results, opt_models = {}, {}
    for name in _OPT_NAMES:
        print(f"Training: {name} ...", end=" ", flush=True)
        cb    = TestAccHistory(X_test, y_test)
        model = _build_opt_model()
        model.compile(optimizer=_make_opt(name),
                      loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
                      metrics=["accuracy"])
        hist = model.fit(X_train, y_train,
                         validation_data=(X_val, y_val),
                         epochs=OPT_EPOCHS, batch_size=OPT_BATCH_SIZE,
                         callbacks=[cb], verbose=0)
        _, test_acc = model.evaluate(X_test, y_test, verbose=0)
        y_pred = np.argmax(model.predict(X_test, verbose=0), axis=1).tolist()
        opt_results[name] = hist.history
        opt_results[name]["test_accuracy"]      = test_acc
        opt_results[name]["test_acc_per_epoch"] = cb.test_accs
        opt_results[name]["test_predictions"]   = y_pred
        opt_models[name] = model
        print(f"done  (val_acc = {hist.history['val_accuracy'][-1]:.3f}  |  test_acc = {test_acc:.3f})")

    OPT_SAVE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(_opt_results_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump(opt_results, f)
    for name, model in opt_models.items():
        model.save(OPT_SAVE_DIR / f"model_{name}.keras")
    print(f"\nSaved to  {OPT_SAVE_DIR.resolve()}")

ax.set_ylim(0, max(opt_test_accs) * 1.15)
ax.set_ylabel("accuracy  (test set)")
ax.set_title(f"Optimiser comparison — test set accuracy  (after {OPT_EPOCHS} epochs)\n"
             f"dataset: {DATASET}  |  batch: {OPT_BATCH_SIZE}")
ax.grid(False)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# ── Graph 4a: Confusion matrix — SGD ─────────────────────────────────────────

def _plot_confusion_matrix(name):
    y_pred = np.array(opt_results[name]["test_predictions"])
    cm     = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
    thresh = cm.max() / 2

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 7))
    im = ax.imshow(cm, cmap="Blues")
    ax.set_xticks(range(NUM_CLASSES))
    ax.set_yticks(range(NUM_CLASSES))
    ax.set_xticklabels(CLASS_NAMES, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=9)
    ax.set_yticklabels(CLASS_NAMES, fontsize=9)
    ax.set_xlabel("predicted")
    ax.set_ylabel("true")
    ax.set_title(f"Confusion matrix — {name}  (test acc = {opt_results[name]['test_accuracy']:.3f})\n"
                 f"dataset: {DATASET}  |  batch: {OPT_BATCH_SIZE}  |  epochs: {OPT_EPOCHS}")
    for i in range(NUM_CLASSES):
        for j in range(NUM_CLASSES):
            ax.text(j, i, str(cm[i, j]),
                    ha="center", va="center", fontsize=8,
                    color="white" if cm[i, j] > thresh else "black")
    fig.colorbar(im, fraction=0.046, pad=0.04)
    plt.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

_plot_confusion_matrix("SGD")

Observations:

  • SGD (with momentum): Converges steadily but typically slower at the start compared to adaptive methods. Momentum helps it accumulate speed along consistent gradient directions.
  • RMSProp: Adapts the learning rate per parameter — usually converges faster than plain SGD on image data where different features have very different gradient magnitudes.
  • Adam: Combines momentum and per-parameter scaling — often reaches a good accuracy quickly and sustains it. Generally the most reliable default for fully connected networks.

The confusion matrices show which classes each optimiser struggles with most — look for rows with mass spread across multiple columns (true class being misclassified everywhere).

Do not treat these rankings as universal. Changing the learning rate, architecture, or dataset can reverse the order.

3. Batch Size¶

Each gradient update step can use a different amount of data:

Variant Batch size Gradient quality Loss curve
Stochastic GD 1 sample Very noisy — 1 sample per step Extremely jagged
Mini-Batch GD small subset Noisy but directional Jagged but trending down
Full-Batch GD all data Exact — no sampling noise Perfectly smooth

The x-axis is iterations (gradient update steps), not epochs — this makes all three directly comparable since each method takes exactly the same number of steps.

A subset of the training data is used so full-batch GD remains fast. The custom tf.GradientTape loop gives precise control over the x-axis.

In [87]:
# ── Batch size hyperparameters — edit these to experiment ─────────────────────
N_BATCH_SAMPLES = 5000    # training subset — keeps full-batch fast
N_ITERS         = 300     # gradient update steps (same for all three methods)
BATCH_LR        = 0.01    # fixed LR — same optimiser (SGD), only batch size changes

BS_STOCHASTIC = 1
BS_MINIBATCH  = 128
BS_FULLBATCH  = N_BATCH_SAMPLES   # all available samples = true full-batch
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

BATCH_CONFIGS = {
    f"Stochastic GD  (bs=1)":                (BS_STOCHASTIC, "#d62728"),
    f"Mini-Batch GD  (bs={BS_MINIBATCH})":   (BS_MINIBATCH,  "#2ca02c"),
    f"Full-Batch GD  (bs={BS_FULLBATCH})":   (BS_FULLBATCH,  "#1f77b4"),
}

BATCH_SAVE_DIR = pathlib.Path(
    f"saved/batch_experiment/"
    f"iters{N_ITERS}_lr{_lr_str(BATCH_LR)}_N{N_BATCH_SAMPLES}"
)
_batch_results_file = BATCH_SAVE_DIR / "batch_results.json"

def _batch_cache_valid():
    if not _batch_results_file.exists():
        return False
    with open(_batch_results_file) as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    return len(data) == len(BATCH_CONFIGS) and all(
        len(v) == N_ITERS for v in data.values()
    )

if _batch_cache_valid():
    print(f"Saved results found — loading from  {BATCH_SAVE_DIR}\n")
    with open(_batch_results_file) as f:
        batch_results = json.load(f)
    for label, losses in batch_results.items():
        print(f"  {label:<42}  final_loss = {losses[-1]:.4f}")

else:
    print("No saved results — running gradient descent loops.\n")

    # fixed subset so full-batch stays fast and all methods see the same data
    _rng_sub = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    _sub_idx = _rng_sub.choice(len(X_train), size=N_BATCH_SAMPLES, replace=False)
    X_sub    = X_train[_sub_idx].reshape(N_BATCH_SAMPLES, -1).astype("float32")
    y_sub    = y_train[_sub_idx].astype("int64")
    X_sub_tf = tf.constant(X_sub)
    y_sub_tf = tf.constant(y_sub)

    def _run_batch_gd(batch_size, n_iters, lr, seed=SEED):
        tf.keras.utils.set_random_seed(seed)
        _rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
        N    = len(X_sub)

        model = keras.Sequential([
            keras.Input(shape=(X_sub.shape[1],)),
            layers.Dense(256, activation="relu"),
            layers.Dense(128, activation="relu"),
            layers.Dense(NUM_CLASSES, activation="softmax"),
        ])
        opt     = keras.optimizers.SGD(learning_rate=lr)
        loss_fn = keras.losses.SparseCategoricalCrossentropy()

        losses = []
        for _ in range(n_iters):
            # full-batch: use every sample; otherwise sample randomly
            idx     = np.arange(N) if batch_size >= N else _rng.integers(0, N, size=batch_size)
            X_batch = tf.gather(X_sub_tf, idx)
            y_batch = tf.gather(y_sub_tf, idx)
            with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
                loss = loss_fn(y_batch, model(X_batch, training=True))
            grads = tape.gradient(loss, model.trainable_variables)
            opt.apply_gradients(zip(grads, model.trainable_variables))
            losses.append(float(loss.numpy()))
        return losses

    batch_results = {}
    for label, (bs, _) in BATCH_CONFIGS.items():
        print(f"Running: {label} ...", end=" ", flush=True)
        losses = _run_batch_gd(bs, N_ITERS, BATCH_LR)
        batch_results[label] = losses
        print(f"done  (final loss = {losses[-1]:.4f})")

    BATCH_SAVE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(_batch_results_file, "w") as f:
        json.dump(batch_results, f)
    print(f"\nSaved to  {BATCH_SAVE_DIR.resolve()}")

# ── Graph: Loss vs iterations ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

iters_x = range(N_ITERS)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
for label, (_, col) in BATCH_CONFIGS.items():
    losses = batch_results[label]
    # stochastic is very noisy — plot faint raw + bold rolling average
    if "Stochastic" in label:
        ax.plot(iters_x, losses, color=col, linewidth=0.6, alpha=0.35)
        window  = 20
        smooth  = np.convolve(losses, np.ones(window) / window, mode="valid")
        ax.plot(range(window - 1, N_ITERS), smooth,
                color=col, linewidth=2, label=label + "  (smoothed)")
    else:
        ax.plot(iters_x, losses, color=col, linewidth=2, label=label)

ax.set_xlabel("iterations  (gradient update steps)")
ax.set_ylabel("cross-entropy loss")
ax.set_title(f"Loss vs iterations — batch size comparison\n"
             f"dataset: {DATASET}  |  N={N_BATCH_SAMPLES}  |  optimiser: SGD  |  lr={BATCH_LR}")
ax.legend(fontsize=10)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

Observations:

  • Stochastic GD (bs=1): Each step uses a single random sample — the loss jumps wildly because one sample is an extremely noisy estimate of the true gradient. The faint raw curve and bold smoothed average are both shown in red.

    • Advantages: extremely fast per-step updates; computationally cheap; the noise can actually help escape local minima that full-batch GD would get stuck in.
    • Disadvantages: VERY noisy; unstable; oscillatory — the parameter path wanders erratically and convergence is hard to guarantee.

  • Mini-Batch GD (bs=128): Averaging over 128 samples per step gives a much more reliable gradient direction — the curve trends downward with moderate noise. This is the practical default in deep learning: it keeps most of stochastic GD's speed while dramatically reducing the instability.

  • Full-Batch GD (bs=5000): Every step uses all available data — the gradient is exact and the loss decreases smoothly and monotonically. No noise, no oscillation, but each step is expensive and it cannot escape local minima once it falls in.

The noise is NOT always bad.

The stochasticity can:

  • help escape local minima,
  • help escape saddle points,
  • improve exploration of parameter space.

This is actually one reason why SGD-based methods work so well in deep learning.

The key trade-off is noise vs. cost per step: stochastic steps are cheapest but noisiest; full-batch steps are most accurate but expensive. Mini-batch sits in the middle and is why batch_size=32–256 is the standard choice in practice.
